reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any normed additive group with a second-countable topology and its Borel measurable structure, let F be any normed additive group, and let mu and nu be any measures on E. Let g : E → F, let b be a nonnegative real number, and let r be any real number. Assume that g is Lipschitz with constant b, that x ↦ ‖g(x)‖² is integrable with respect to nu, and that W₂(mu,nu)² ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(r²), where W₂ is the extended nonnegative quadratic Wasserstein distance defined as the square root of the infimum of quadratic coupling costs. Then x ↦ ‖g(x)‖² is integrable with respect to mu, and ∫ ‖g(x)‖² dmu(x) ≤ 2 ∫ ‖g(x)‖² dnu(x) + 2 b² r².
objects: Two measures mu and nu on E; a Lipschitz map g from E to F; a nonnegative Lipschitz constant b; a real parameter r; the real-valued squared-norm function x ↦ ‖g(x)‖²; and the quadratic Wasserstein distance between the measures.
domains: E is a normed additive group with a second-countable topology and its Borel measurable structure. F is a normed additive group. mu and nu are measures on E. g : E → F, b : NNReal, and r : ℝ. The Wasserstein bound is an inequality in the extended nonnegative reals; the final integral inequality is real-valued.
quantifiers: For every E and F with the stated structures, every pair of measures mu and nu on E, every map g : E → F, every b in NNReal, and every real r, the three assumptions imply both conclusions.
assumptions: g is globally Lipschitz with constant b; x ↦ ‖g(x)‖² is nu-integrable; and the square of the quadratic Wasserstein distance from mu to nu is at most ENNReal.ofReal(r²). No probability-measure, completeness, finite-dimensionality, or nonnegativity-of-r assumption is explicitly present.
conclusion: The squared-norm function x ↦ ‖g(x)‖² is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is at most twice its nu-integral plus 2 b² r², with b coerced to a real number.
scopes: Integrability is global over E, not local or restricted to compact subsets. The conclusion transfers an integrability property and a quantitative integral bound from nu to mu. g is an ordinary pointwise map, not an equivalence class or selected representative. No pointwise bound on ‖g(x)‖² is asserted. r may have either sign because only r² appears. No particular coupling or attainment of the infimum defining Wasserstein distance is assumed.
constant_dependencies: The bound uses the universal numerical coefficient 2, the incoming squared-norm integral under nu, the squared Lipschitz constant b², and r². No dimension-dependent constant, chosen base point, or additive offset involving g at a point appears.
